name: return_constant_zero
description: Stores zero into a stack-frame slot and returns that same value. It touches no libraries or other state.

name: write_with_elapsed_time_check
description: Writes a buffer through the file write call and reads the system time before and after. It returns one if fewer bytes were written than requested, ninety-nine if the write succeeded but took longer than twenty-eight time units, and zero otherwise.

name: open_or_close_printer_handle
description: With a zero argument it closes the stored handle if one is set and returns zero. Otherwise it opens the device named in the referenced text, which is the printer port, and returns zero on success or one on failure.

name: set_console_reset_state
description: A zero argument clears the second flag and closes the first stage. A nonzero argument opens the first stage if needed, then sends a two-byte escape sequence of escape followed by a lowercase c through the write routine and sets the second flag on success. It returns the second flag.

name: write_buffer_then_escape_sequence
description: Writes the given buffer when the length is positive, and if that write returns zero, or the length is not positive, sends a two-byte escape sequence of escape followed by an uppercase E. It returns the result of the final write.

name: format_memory_status_report
description: Reads the free public memory size and clamps it against a stored limit, then builds a status line in a 64-byte buffer using the referenced labels for maximum, bytes free and bytes used. It returns the memory amount it chose to report.

name: allocate_remembered_memory
description: Allocates a block of the requested size and records it in the shared remember list so that all such blocks can be freed in one call. It returns nothing.

name: open_custom_screen_and_window
description: With a zero argument it closes the window and then the screen if they are open. Otherwise it opens a one-plane screen 640 units wide and 187 tall, then a window 640 units wide and 176 tall on that screen. It returns one or two for the respective failures and zero on success.

name: setup_console_resources_and_icons
description: Opens the libraries named in the referenced text and the console device, temporarily changes one preference byte and restores it afterwards, creates a message port with a signal, copies a 48-byte block into a global, and loads the disk icon for a referenced name. It returns zero on success or one of three distinct error codes.

name: release_console_and_icon_resources
description: Reverses the setup routine by releasing, in order, the disk icon, the icon library, the remembered allocations, the message port, the signal, the console device, and the library opened at setup. Each release is skipped when its handle is empty.

name: handle_f_prefixed_path_argument
description: Resets a stored value to minus one, then if the first argument is at least two and the second points to a string starting with the letter F in either case followed by a slash, it passes the rest of that string to another routine and resets the value on failure. It then runs a main step, a cleanup step if the main step returns zero, and a final step, returning the main step's result.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: Only bad instruction data was decoded as code here, so the routine has no meaningful behaviour. It is not a usable routine.

name: call_current_time_function
description: Calls the system library function that returns the current time, reached through the library base stored in a global variable. It returns nothing.

name: call_open_screen_function
description: Calls the system library function that opens a screen, reached through the library base stored in a global variable. It passes its arguments through unchanged.

name: call_free_remember_function
description: Calls the system library function that frees a remember list of allocations, reached through the library base stored in a global variable. It passes its arguments through unchanged.

name: copy_null_terminated_string
description: Copies a zero-terminated byte string from the second argument into the first, byte by byte including the terminator, and returns the destination pointer.

name: copy_string_with_length_limit
description: Copies up to the given count of bytes from the source string into the destination, stopping early at a zero byte. It then writes a zero terminator at the end of the copied bytes and returns the destination pointer.

name: zero_indirect_byte_return_value
description: Writes a zero byte through a pointer read from the stack frame, then returns a long value read from the caller's argument area. Since no parameters are named in the code, the meaning of the returned value is unclear.

name: append_null_terminated_string
description: Finds the end of the destination string by calling a routine that returns its length, then copies the zero-terminated source string onto that end, byte by byte including its terminator. It returns the destination pointer.

name: append_string_with_length_limit
description: Finds the end of the destination string by calling a routine that returns its length, then copies up to the given count of bytes from the source, stopping early at a zero byte. It writes a zero terminator at the end and returns the destination pointer.

name: clear_pointed_byte_return_value
description: Writes a zero byte through a pointer read from the stack frame, then returns a long value read from the caller's argument area. The parameters are not named in the code, so the returned value's meaning is unclear.

name: count_string_bytes
description: Counts the bytes from a given pointer forward until a zero byte is reached, and returns that count without including the terminator.

name: format_integer_as_decimal
description: Writes the given integer as a zero-terminated decimal string into the destination buffer, limited by the buffer size argument, and returns the number of characters written. If the buffer size is below two it writes an empty string and returns zero.

name: parse_signed_decimal_string
description: Reads an optional plus or minus sign followed by decimal digits, using a character-class table to recognise digits and accumulating the value. It stores the result through the second argument and returns the number of characters consumed, including any sign.

name: find_first_character_in_string
description: Walks a zero-terminated string and returns a pointer to the first byte equal to the given character, or a null pointer if none is found before the terminator.

name: find_next_delimiter_match
description: Advances a read position held in the caller's frame through a zero-terminated string and returns a pointer to the next byte matching the delimiter stored in the same frame, or a null pointer when the string ends.

name: forward_arguments_to_inner_routine
description: Passes its two arguments unchanged to another routine and returns nothing. It contains no other logic.

name: find_last_character_in_string
description: Scans a zero-terminated string and returns a pointer to the last byte equal to the given character, or a null pointer if no byte matches.

name: return_frame_local_value
description: Reads a long value from the stack frame and returns it without writing anything. The meaning of the value depends on the caller's frame layout, which is not visible here.

name: initialise_global_table_slots
description: Calls a routine twenty times and passes each result, together with an address into a global table, to another routine. It then calls that routine for each index up to a count held in a global, and finally passes its two arguments to a third routine.

name: divide_unsigned_longwords
description: Divides the first unsigned 32-bit value by the second using a bit-by-bit shift and subtract loop, and returns the quotient. A zero divisor or zero dividend produces zero.

name: empty_stub_function
description: Returns immediately with no observable effect on memory or I/O, so it behaves as a no-op. The decompiled body is a plain return.

name: find_free_record_slot
description: Scans a table of 24-byte records for the first one whose flag byte is clear, stopping at the end of the table. If no record is free it returns zero; otherwise it passes the two arguments and the free record to another routine and returns that routine's result.

name: forward_record_when_not_end
description: Returns zero when the record pointer taken from its stack frame equals the end of the record table. Otherwise it calls another routine with three frame arguments and returns that routine's result.

name: forward_record_arguments
description: Passes three arguments taken from its stack frame to another routine and returns nothing.

name: open_file_with_mode_string
description: Closes any file already attached to the record, then parses a file mode string whose first letter selects read, write or append, whose second letter selects an extra mode flag, and whose plus sign selects update. It opens the named file and fills in the record, returning the record or a null pointer on failure.

name: open_file_from_frame_arguments
description: Opens a file using the mode letter and plus sign found in its stack frame, following the same logic as the sibling open routine. It fills in the record stored in the frame and returns it, or a null pointer if the open fails.

name: open_file_for_appending
description: Opens the named file for appending with the flags it was given, seeks to the end of the file, and fills in the record stored in its frame. It returns the record, or a null pointer if the open fails.

name: seek_frame_handle_to_end
description: Moves the file position of the handle held in the stack frame to the end of the file, then fills in the record stored in the frame and returns it.

name: finalise_file_record_fields
description: Sets a mode value of two in its frame, fills the record's buffer pointers and mode byte, and applies an extra flag bit when a table entry is set. It returns the record and opens no file itself.

name: open_file_with_access_flags
description: Opens the file using the access flag held in its stack frame, and if the open fails returns a null pointer. Otherwise it stores the handle and a mode byte in the record, sets the record's buffer fields, and returns the record.

name: open_named_file_and_record
description: Calls the open routine with the file name and mode values from the stack frame and returns a null pointer if that fails. On success it stores the handle and a mode byte, fills in the record's fields and returns the record.

name: fill_record_with_mode
description: Sets a mode byte in the stack frame from a flag, then fills the record's buffer pointers and mode byte and returns the record. No file is opened.

name: fill_record_with_fixed_mode
description: Sets a fixed mode value of one in the stack frame, then fills the record's buffer pointers and mode byte and returns the record. No file is opened.

name: open_file_for_writing_record
description: Opens the named file for writing with create or replace behaviour and the protection values in the code. It stores the handle and a mode byte in the record and returns it, or a null pointer if the open fails.

name: open_file_for_read_write
description: Opens the named file for combined read and write access with create behaviour, then stores the handle and a mode byte in the record. It returns the record, or a null pointer if the open fails.

name: fill_record_mode_without_open
description: Sets the record's mode byte to a read-write or write value depending on a flag, fills the buffer pointers and returns the record. No file is opened.

name: fill_record_fixed_mode_two
description: Sets a fixed mode value of two in the stack frame, then fills the record's buffer pointers and mode byte and returns the record. No file is opened.

name: return_constant_zero_result
description: Returns zero without any other effect. It is a constant-result stub.

name: fill_record_fields_from_frame
description: Fills the record's buffer pointers and mode byte from values in its stack frame, applying a flag bit when a table entry is set, and returns the record. No file is opened.

name: reset_record_fields_and_return
description: Clears a link field of the record, sets its buffer pointers and mode byte from the stack frame, and returns the record. No file is opened.

name: clear_object_links
description: Releases the record's contents: if one flag bit is set it calls a routine with the record, and if the masked flags are clear and a second stored value is present it calls another routine with the two stored fields. It then clears the pointer fields and flag byte, and passes a byte field to a third routine.

name: lookup_active_file_slot
description: Checks that the index argument lies within the slot table and that the slot's flag byte has its top bit set. If so it returns a pointer to that slot's entry; otherwise it records an invalid-slot error code and returns a null pointer.

name: allocate_file_slot_and_open
description: Finds a free entry in the slot table and sets its flag byte from the requested access mode and option bits. It optionally deletes the existing file, opens the named file, stores the handle, and returns the slot index. On failure it records an error code, clears the slot, and returns minus one.

name: open_file_into_frame_slot
description: Works like the slot allocator but takes the slot index from its stack frame, failing with a no-free-slot error if that index is past the table end. Otherwise it sets the slot's flags from the mode and option values, optionally deletes the file, opens it and stores the handle, returning the index or minus one on failure.

name: open_file_into_slot_flags
description: Sets the slot's flags from the mode and option bits in its stack frame, optionally deletes the file, opens it, and stores the handle in the slot. It returns the frame index on success or minus one on failure.

name: open_file_slot_after_flags
description: Marks the slot active and sets its access flags from the mode bits in the stack frame, deletes the file if requested, opens it and stores the handle. It returns the frame value on success or minus one on failure.

name: open_file_write_access_slot
description: Sets the write-type access flag on the slot, with the optional bit from the stack frame, deletes the file when requested, opens it with create or replace behaviour, and stores the handle. It returns the frame value, or minus one on failure.

name: open_file_write_flag_slot
description: Sets the write-type access flag on the slot, deletes the file when a delete option is present, opens it, and stores the handle. It returns the frame value on success or minus one on failure.

name: open_file_update_access_slot
description: Sets the combined read and write access flags on the slot, with the optional bit from the stack frame, deletes the file when requested, opens it and stores the handle. It returns the frame value on success or minus one on failure.

name: open_file_update_flag_slot
description: Sets the combined read and write flags on the slot, deletes the file if requested, opens it with the mode from the stack frame and stores the handle. It returns the frame value, or minus one after clearing the slot on failure.

name: reject_invalid_slot_argument
description: Clears the slot's flag byte, records an invalid-argument error code and returns minus one. It is the failure exit used when the requested access mode is not recognised.

name: delete_and_open_slot_file
description: Deletes the file when the option bit is set, opens it using the mode derived from the flags, and stores the handle in the slot. It returns the frame value; on failure it records the I/O error, clears the slot and returns minus one.

name: open_existing_file_into_slot
description: Opens the named file for reading in the fixed existing-file mode and stores the handle in the slot. It returns the frame value, or on failure records the I/O error, clears the slot and returns minus one.

name: return_frame_index_value
description: Returns the long value from the stack frame unchanged, without any other effect.

name: split_open_flags_and_forward
description: Passes the first argument with a combined set of open mode bits and the high flag bit of the second argument, and passes the second argument with that high flag bit cleared to another routine. It returns nothing.

name: read_bytes_from_slot
description: Reads up to the given count of bytes into the buffer from the file attached to the slot. A negative count or an unknown slot records an invalid-argument error and returns minus one; a failed read records the I/O error and returns the read result.

name: read_bytes_into_frame_buffer
description: Reads the number of bytes given in its stack frame into the buffer, using the file handle stored in the frame. It records an I/O error code when the read fails and returns the number of bytes read.

name: write_bytes_to_slot
description: Writes the given number of bytes from the buffer to the file attached to the slot, first seeking to the end of the file when the slot's append flag is set. An invalid count or unknown slot records an invalid-argument error and returns minus one; a failed write records the I/O error and returns minus one.

name: seek_file_with_offset_table
description: Looks up the file attached to the slot and, when the index is below three, seeks to the position stored in a global table for that index. It records an I/O error if that seek fails, then performs a zero-offset seek and returns its result. An unknown slot or out-of-range index records an invalid-argument error and returns minus one.

name: close_file_slot
description: Looks up the slot and returns minus one if it is missing. If a flag bit is set it returns zero without closing anything. Otherwise it closes the file, records any I/O error with an error code and returns minus one on error, then clears the slot's flag byte.

name: delete_named_file
description: Deletes the file with the given name. On failure it records the I/O error and an error code and returns minus one; otherwise it returns zero.

name: return_zero_status_stub
description: Returns zero with no other effect. It reports success without performing any file operation.

name: open_global_file_handle
description: Opens the file named by a global string in the existing-file mode and stores the handle in a global variable. It returns nothing and does not check the result.

name: read_one_byte_with_pushback
description: Returns a byte previously held in a global variable, clearing that holding. Otherwise it reads one byte from the open file handle held in a global and returns it, first making sure the handle is available.

name: read_one_byte_from_handle
description: Reads a single byte from the open file handle held in a global variable into a stack slot, and returns that byte. It does not check how many bytes were read.

name: write_one_byte_to_handle
description: Makes sure the file handle is available, writes the single byte argument to the open file, and returns that byte rather than the write result.

name: forward_two_arguments_onward
description: Passes its two arguments unchanged to another routine and returns nothing. It adds no logic of its own.

name: read_next_buffered_byte
description: Returns the next byte from a buffered stream and refills the buffer through another routine when it is empty. It returns minus one when the stream has an error or end flag set or the refill fails, and it sets those status flags when a refill returns zero or fails.

name: read_next_byte_from_frame
description: Works like its sibling buffered reader but takes the stream from its stack frame. It returns the next byte, or minus one when the stream is in an error or end state or a refill fails.

name: read_next_byte_with_refill
description: Refills the stream's buffer through another routine, using the buffer size stored in the stream unless an unbuffered flag is set, then returns the next byte. It returns minus one when an error or end flag is set or the refill fails.

name: refill_then_read_next_byte
description: Returns minus one if a status bit is set. Otherwise it marks the stream as in use, refills its buffer through another routine using the stored size, records error or short-read flags, and returns the next buffered byte.

name: refill_and_read_stream_byte
description: Marks the stream as buffered, refills it through another routine using the stored size, and records error flags for a failed or short read. It returns the next byte, or minus one when an error or end flag is set.

name: read_byte_from_buffer
description: Takes the next byte from the stream's buffer and advances the position. When the buffer count has run out it calls a refill routine first, then returns the byte.

name: forward_stream_argument_call
description: Passes the stream pointer from its stack frame to another routine and returns nothing.

name: write_byte_to_buffered_stream
description: Writes one byte into a buffered output stream, first flushing the pending buffer through another routine when the buffer is full. A failed or short flush sets an error or short-write flag, and the routine returns minus one on error or the byte written otherwise.

name: allocate_stream_buffer
description: Allocates a buffer of the size stored in a global variable and records it as the stream's buffer pointer, clearing the status bits and counters. If allocation fails it records an out-of-memory error and returns minus one; if a buffer already exists and a reset flag is clear it returns zero without change.

name: shift_global_value_left_three
description: Loads a global variable, shifts it left by three bits so it is multiplied by eight, and returns the result.

name: forward_value_twice
description: Passes its 32-bit argument to another routine twice, once as each of two arguments, and returns nothing.

name: allocate_from_free_list
description: Searches a linked list of free memory blocks for the first block large enough for the requested size. An exact fit is unlinked, a larger block is split, and the free total is reduced. If no block fits it asks another routine for more memory and retries once, returning a null pointer if that fails; a non-positive size also returns a null pointer.

name: forward_with_repeated_second_argument
description: Passes its first argument, and its second argument again as a third, to another routine and returns nothing.

name: return_block_to_free_list
description: Inserts a block of the given size into the sorted free list, using its computed address to find the position. It merges the block with an adjacent free neighbour where possible, or links it in as a new node, and adds the size to the free total. An overlapping or inconsistent block is rejected with minus one, as is a non-positive size.

name: check_break_signal_and_report
description: Reads the break signal bits and returns zero if neither relevant bit is set. Otherwise, when a global flag is set, it writes a caret followed by the letter D or C depending on which bit was set, then a newline, calls a routine for each index up to a global count, and returns the result of a final call.

name: divide_signed_longwords
description: Divides the first signed 32-bit value by the second using a restoring shift and subtract loop on their magnitudes, giving the quotient the sign of the xor of the operands. It returns zero when either operand is zero.

name: enable_dma_and_run_loop
description: Writes a DMA control value with the enable bit set, then makes setup calls before entering a loop that updates words in a table and checks a status bit on each pass. The decompiled code is truncated partway through, so the rest of the routine cannot be described from the evidence.

name: store_byte_and_call_pointer
description: Stores a fixed byte value into a memory location, calls a routine through a pointer read from a table entry, then sets a global variable to 255 and returns the two register values unchanged. The called routine and the written location are not identified in the evidence.

name: configure_blitter_operation_fields
description: Clears two halfword fields and writes fixed control words into the structure at the register address, stores a global value in one long field, then calls routines that program the blitter registers listed in the evidence. The structure layout is inferred only from the field offsets.

name: configure_second_blitter_operation
description: Writes the same kind of control fields as its sibling routine, with a different final control word, stores the same global value in one long field, then calls routines that program the blitter registers. The structure layout is inferred only from the field offsets.

name: repeat_call_for_count
description: Calls another routine repeatedly, decrementing the count held in a register on each pass, and stops once the count goes below zero. It therefore runs one more time than the starting count.

name: scan_pattern_counters_until_asterisk
description: Walks a byte string, stopping at an asterisk and returning two counters as a pair. A plus sign adds sixteen to the first counter, a left parenthesis subtracts sixteen from it, and a right parenthesis adds sixteen to the second counter. Any other character is passed to a check routine and retried after a short bounded loop of calls that returns early when a status bit is set.

name: invoke_seven_routines_in_sequence
description: Calls seven other routines one after another with no arguments or other logic, then returns.

name: reduce_remainder_by_divisor
description: Subtracts the divisor from the dividend up to eight times, stopping once the remainder is smaller than the divisor, then passes the remainder to another routine. The inputs come from fixed registers rather than named parameters.

name: invoke_five_routines_in_sequence
description: Calls five other routines one after another with no arguments or other logic, then returns.

name: reduce_remainder_by_divisor
description: Subtracts the divisor from the dividend up to eight times, stopping once the remainder is smaller than the divisor, then passes the remainder to another routine. The inputs come from fixed registers rather than named parameters.

name: test_axis_ranges_overlap
description: Compares 16-bit position and size values held in registers on the horizontal axis, then the vertical axis. It returns one when the two ranges overlap on both axes and zero when they are separated; the register inputs are unnamed, so this reading is inferred from the comparisons.

name: check_axis_distance_within_limit
description: Computes a 16-bit distance from two register values, choosing the direction by a sign test, and returns one when that distance is below a limit held in another register. Otherwise it returns zero.

name: compare_negated_value_limit
description: Returns zero when a limit register is at most the negation of a second register value, and one otherwise.

name: zero_longword_block_unrolled
description: Writes zero to a contiguous run of more than two hundred longwords in memory using individual stores with no loop.

name: clear_longword_region_backward
description: Clears a memory region of longwords by an outer loop of fourteen passes, each writing zeros with unrolled stores. The decompiled code is truncated, so the full extent of the region is not visible.

name: clear_thirty_two_longwords
description: Writes zero to thirty-two consecutive longwords starting at a fixed memory address, then returns.

name: read_joystick_port_status_flags
description: Reads two hardware input bytes, one per joystick port, and sets flag bits in a stored status value for each port's button or direction state. It then stores the combined status and an update byte in memory.

name: wait_for_interrupt_request_bit
description: Sets a status global to a single flag bit and then busy-waits until that bit reads as set. The loop only exits when another part of the program or hardware changes the global, which fits waiting on an interrupt request.

name: wait_until_status_bit_set
description: Busy-waits until a particular status bit in a global variable reads as set, then returns.

name: wait_for_dma_status_clear
description: Busy-waits while one status bit in a global variable is set, then writes a fixed value with a single high bit into that variable. The DMA control registers in the evidence suggest it waits for a DMA state to clear.

name: toggle_between_two_timing_values
description: Alternates a global variable between two fixed values on successive calls: a value other than the larger one is set to the larger, and the larger one is replaced by the smaller.

name: blit_masked_add_four_planes
description: Clears destination bits wherever any of the four source words has a set bit, then adds the source words into the four destination planes. It loops over the rows and columns given by its counters, advancing the pointers by a row stride.

name: blit_or_then_clear_planes
description: Combines four source words per column by OR and ORs the result into two destination planes, while clearing those same bits from the other two planes. Its loops are driven by row and column counters.

name: blit_or_clear_planes_stride
description: Performs the same combine-and-clear operation as its sibling on four bitplanes, with the source and destination pointers advanced by a different row stride in the outer loop.

name: copy_four_plane_words_forward
description: Copies four source words per column into four destination planes at fixed plane offsets, looping over the given row and column counts and advancing the destination by a row stride.

name: copy_four_plane_words_backward
description: Copies four source words per column into four destination planes at fixed plane offsets, like its sibling, but steps the destination backward between rows.

name: compute_bitplane_byte_address
description: Returns the address of a byte in a bitplane buffer, computed as the buffer base plus the row multiplied by forty bytes plus a column offset taken from the upper bits of the first register.

name: copy_sixteen_words_to_tables
description: Copies sixteen words from the source pointer into a table in memory. When a global variable is nonzero it also stores a second copy with a fixed value added, then returns; otherwise it runs a variant copy loop whose tail is not fully shown.

name: copy_sixteen_words_indexed_row
description: Selects a source row from a global value, computed as its tenth part scaled by a row stride, then copies sixteen words from that row into a table. When the global is nonzero it also stores a second copy with a fixed value added, like its sibling routine.

name: run_copper_colour_update_loop
description: Sets display control values and a colour register, then repeatedly decodes signed byte pairs from a buffer and passes each pair to another routine, checking a stop bit on every pass. The decompiled code runs beyond the portion shown, so this covers only the setup and the start of the loop.

name: call_fourteen_routines_in_sequence
description: Makes fourteen calls to other routines in sequence, with no arguments or other logic: one to a fixed routine, five to another fixed routine and eight to unnamed routines.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: Only bad instruction data was decoded as code here, so the routine has no meaningful behaviour. It is not a usable routine.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: Only bad instruction data was decoded as code here, so the routine has no meaningful behaviour. It is not a usable routine.

name: copy_indexed_table_entry_bytes
description: Clamps a register index to nine, locates the matching thirty-two byte entry in a fixed table, and copies eight bytes of it into a destination buffer.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: Only bad instruction data was decoded as code here, so the routine has no meaningful behaviour. It is not a usable routine.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: Only a call followed by bad instruction data was decoded here, so no meaningful routine behaviour can be recovered.

name: clear_four_plane_column_block
description: When a global counter lies within a small range, it clears sixteen rows of four bitplane words in a block at a fixed offset from the buffer. Outside that range it does nothing. It calls another routine first in both cases.

name: copy_table_entry_for_index
description: Clamps a global index to nine, locates the matching thirty-two byte table entry, and copies eight bytes of it into a destination at a fixed offset from the buffer base.

name: copy_table_entry_secondary_index
description: Clamps a second global index to nine, locates the matching thirty-two byte table entry, and copies eight bytes of it into a destination at a different fixed offset from the buffer base.

name: copy_table_entry_for_index
description: Clamps a global index to nine, locates the matching thirty-two byte table entry, and copies eight bytes of it into a destination at a fixed offset from the buffer base.

name: copy_table_entry_for_index
description: Clamps a global index to nine, locates the matching thirty-two byte table entry, and copies eight bytes of it into a destination at a fixed offset from the buffer base.

name: setup_blitter_copy_registers
description: Calls another routine, then writes blitter control words, first and last word masks, modulo values and source and destination pointers into the hardware blitter registers. It finishes by writing a fixed blit size word, which starts the operation.

name: setup_blitter_alternate_size_registers
description: Writes the same blitter control words, masks, modulo values and pointers as its sibling routine, but starts the blit with a different fixed size word.

name: fill_blitter_parameter_structure
description: Writes the same blitter control words and pointers as its sibling routine into a structure addressed by a register rather than into the hardware registers, then starts with a fixed size word. It calls another routine first.

name: copy_overlay_block_for_index
description: Copies 236 words from a table row selected by a global index into memory starting at the address of this routine, overwriting the code there. Each pass advances both the source and destination pointers.

name: accumulate_byte_checksum_step
description: Adds three register values and the byte at the current buffer position, returns the low byte of the sum, and moves the position forward by two. It stops advancing once a fixed end address is reached.

name: swap_fifty_longwords
description: Swaps fifty longwords one pair at a time between the area pointed to by an address register and a fixed area in memory.

name: record_minimum_value_seen
description: Stores the argument in a global variable when that variable is unset or the argument is at most its current value, and clears a flag byte at the same time. Otherwise it leaves both unchanged.

name: invoke_two_routines_in_sequence
description: Calls two other routines one after another with no arguments and returns. One of the called routines points the copper at a new copper list.

name: call_and_pass_registers_through
description: Calls another routine, then returns the two register values it was given unchanged as a pair.

name: run_countdown_interrupt_wait_loop
description: Calls three setup routines, then runs a ninety-nine pass countdown loop. Each pass calls another routine with values computed from the countdown, sets a status global and calls two routines around it, and makes one further call when a second global flag is nonzero.

name: invoke_two_routines_in_sequence
description: Calls two other routines one after another with no arguments and returns. One of the called routines points the copper at a new copper list.

name: expand_table_rows_to_planes
description: For each source byte row, looks up an eight-byte aligned entry in a fixed table and copies twenty words from it into four bitplanes at fixed plane offsets. It advances the source by a row stride until the row count runs out.

name: scan_pattern_from_indexed_table
description: Selects a pattern string from a table by a global index and walks it, starting from counters taken from a fixed table row. It returns the two counters when it reaches an asterisk, and it follows the same character rules as its sibling scanner.

name: and_mask_bitplane_words
description: Loops 4000 times, reading one source word and ANDing it into the matching word of each bitplane in a buffer, advancing the buffer pointer on each pass.

name: run_eight_step_display_loop
description: Calls two routines, then runs an eight-pass loop that calls another routine with the loop counter and a second value that steps down by a fixed amount each pass. It makes three further calls after the loop.

name: load_sixteen_palette_entries
description: Loops over sixteen palette words, writing each into the colour registers through one routine. When a flag is nonzero it also calls a second routine on each pass.

name: step_palette_entries_cyclically
description: Cycles through a table of palette words a hundred times, adding a fixed value to each entry before writing it to the colour registers and wrapping at the end of the table.

name: set_timeout_counter_value
description: Stores the value ten thousand in a global counter and returns.

name: set_timeout_counter_value
description: Stores the value ten thousand in a global counter and returns.

name: copy_large_longword_block_forward
description: Copies 5924 longwords one at a time from one fixed memory area to another.

name: copy_large_longword_block_back
description: Copies the same 5924 longwords as its sibling in the opposite direction, from the second memory area back into the first.

name: setup_display_and_copper_registers
description: Writes fixed display window, data fetch, bitplane and colour control registers, then enables DMA and interrupt bits. It points the copper at a new list, stores handler routine addresses and buffer pointers in tables, and returns two values.

name: configure_blit_structure_fixed_size
description: Sets the control words and a fixed pointer value in a blitter structure at the register address, writes a fixed blit size word, and calls another routine before and after the field writes.

name: wait_for_serial_status_flags
description: Sets the serial period register, then polls the serial status for up to 250 passes. It returns the remaining count when the receive flag or transmit-empty flag is seen, clearing the receive request bit in the first case, and returns minus one if the polls run out.

name: poll_port_status_until_ready
description: Repeats a routine until a count reaches zero while checking status flags on a port structure. When the receive flag is set it clears the request bit and returns the port's data byte, when the ready flag is set it returns the data byte, and it returns the count's result otherwise.

name: clear_receive_request_return_byte
description: Writes the receive-interrupt clear value into a port structure's request word, then returns the port's data byte.

name: setup_three_blit_passes
description: Writes blitter control words, masks and modulo values into a structure, then sets up three successive blits by storing a fixed size word and a source and destination pointer for each. It calls another routine to obtain each pointer.

name: merge_bitplane_rows_with_or
description: Repeats ninety-nine times: copies thirty-two longwords into a work area, then ORs groups of four source words into sixteen destination words, and copies a further group pattern. Row and column counts are fixed by the loops.

name: copy_overlay_and_merge_planes
description: Copies 1024 longwords from one fixed area into the code region at the routine's own address, then merges groups of four words from a second area into a destination buffer with OR, 512 words per pass.

name: select_line_octant_and_blit
description: Chooses one of eight direction codes from the signs and sizes of two coordinate differences, as a line-drawing routine would, and computes a modulo value from the larger difference. It then runs a blit with OR merges; the rest of the routine is only partly visible.

name: invoke_four_routines_in_sequence
description: Calls four other routines one after another with no arguments and returns.

name: lookup_sixteen_byte_table_entry
description: Clears a global counter and looks up a sixteen-byte table entry indexed by it. When the entry holds minus one it takes an alternate path; the remaining steps call two routines and are only partly visible.

name: setup_blitter_modulo_and_pointers
description: Calls another routine, then writes blitter control words, a fixed modulo value and source and destination pointers into a blitter structure, followed by a fixed size word. The remaining lines are not visible.

name: configure_full_blitter_transfer
description: Calls another routine, then sets the blitter source, mask, destination and modulo registers and control words for a full transfer. The start offsets are chosen from the two coordinate differences before the blit is started; the decompiled code is partly truncated.

name: initialise_cia_port_registers
description: Writes control values to the CIA port direction and data registers, sets a status global to a fixed value, and clears a flag global.

name: poll_cia_byte_when_flagged
description: Reads a byte from another routine when a status bit is set, rotates it right by one with its low bit moved to the top, marks a flag bit in a structure, and calls another routine. The other branch is not shown in full.

name: step_countdown_state_machine
description: Clears a flag bit in a structure, then steps a countdown held in a global. When the countdown is zero it reloads it to ten, sets the status global to a fixed value and calls a series of other routines; the tail of the routine is partly visible.

name: install_interrupt_handler_and_enable
description: Stores a routine address into a global variable, writes an interrupt enable value that sets the enable bit for particular interrupts, and then writes a value that clears all interrupts.

name: store_interrupt_handler_address
description: Stores the address of a routine into a global variable and returns nothing.

name: conditionally_call_and_set_flag
description: Returns at once unless one flag bit is set in a global variable. When it is set, it calls another routine and then writes the flag bit back into the global.

name: rearm_flag_when_set
description: Returns at once if one flag bit in a global variable is clear; otherwise it writes that flag bit back so the variable holds only that bit.

name: set_status_flag_bit
description: Writes a single flag bit into a global variable, replacing its other bits, and returns.

name: wait_for_status_high_byte
description: Waits for a raster line, then counts a global variable upward with a short delay on each pass, until its high byte reaches a fixed value.

name: store_argument_in_global
description: Stores the value passed in the data register into a global variable and returns.

name: count_passes_until_status_byte
description: Waits for a raster line, then counts passes in a local variable until the high byte of a global variable reaches a fixed value. The rest of the routine is not visible.

name: set_copper_list_and_call
description: Points the copper at a new copper list and makes one other call. The decompiled body is unavailable, so this description rests only on the list of calls.

name: call_and_pass_registers_through
description: Calls another routine, then returns the two register values it was given unchanged as a pair.

name: select_table_pointers_by_flag
description: Checks a flag byte in a structure and chooses between two table addresses depending on it, then processes a sequence of table entries. The rest of the routine is not fully visible.

name: configure_disk_controller_dma
description: Writes disk and audio control and DMA control values, reads the CIA port status, and calls three other routines. The visible part of the body is only partly shown.

name: busy_wait_512_iterations
description: Counts down through a fixed loop of 512 steps with no other work, then returns, giving a short delay.

name: call_and_pass_registers_through
description: Calls another routine, then returns the two register values it was given unchanged as a pair.

name: call_and_pass_registers_through
description: Calls another routine, then returns the two register values it was given unchanged as a pair.

name: call_single_routine_and_return
description: Calls one other routine with no arguments and returns. It adds no logic of its own.

name: call_single_routine_and_return
description: Calls one other routine with no arguments and returns. It adds no logic of its own.

name: call_single_routine_and_return
description: Calls one other routine with no arguments and returns. It adds no logic of its own.

name: call_single_routine_and_return
description: Calls one other routine with no arguments and returns. It adds no logic of its own.

name: initialise_four_channel_structures
description: Sets a flag bit, selects a row from a table using a value returned by another routine, and fills four 48-byte channel structures with fixed initial values and table-derived pointers. It reads the joystick and disk status port while doing this.

name: clear_audio_channel_state
description: Zeroes a series of state variables and sets a few others to fixed constants as part of initialising audio channel state. It touches the audio and DMA control registers in the evidence.

name: set_four_channel_active_flags
description: Sets four flag variables to one, marking four channels as active, and returns.

name: enable_channel_dma_mask
description: When a flag byte is nonzero, builds a DMA enable mask with the bits for four audio channels set and writes it to the state, along with a fixed value. Otherwise it does nothing.

name: set_playback_state_three
description: Sets a global variable and a byte variable to three and returns.

name: dispatch_hunk_records_by_type
description: Reads and decodes a stream of records, comparing type values with AmigaDOS hunk codes to decide how each block is handled, such as loading or relocating code. The routine is long and only partly visible.

name: decode_sound_command_stream
description: Reads command bytes from a stream and updates audio channel state, using a table to derive tone values. The visible code is only the start of a longer routine.

name: decode_sound_command_stream_variant
description: Decodes command bytes from a stream into audio channel state in the same way as its sibling, with the audio and DMA control registers also written in the evidence. The visible part is only the start of the routine.

name: decode_sound_stream_fragment
description: Decodes a stream of command bytes like its sibling routines, updating channel state from a table of tone values. Only the opening portion of the routine is visible.
